# Parkinson's disease — rehabilitation and adjunct therapies

> 8 concept packs from the research run on rehabilitation and adjunct therapies (exercise, physical, speech and occupational therapy, dance, music, acupuncture, cannabis and supplements); 117 of the family's 1,155 claims are grouped under this section in llms-facts.txt. Educational research reference, not medical advice.
> Source: research run parkinson-s-disease-rehabilitation-and-adjunct-therapies-exercise-physical-speech-and-occupational-therapy-dance-music-acupuncture-cannabis-and-supplements · Generated: 2026-11-27 by llms-deep-optimizer v1.2.1 · Mode: family

## Concept packs

- [Run-level pack: Rehabilitation and adjunct therapies](https://llmsx.org/tree/parkinson-s-disease-rehabilitation-and-adjunct-therapies-exercise-physical-speech-and-occupational-therapy-dance-music-acupuncture-cannabis-and-supplements/): Run-level pack covering exercise, physical, speech and occupational therapy, dance, music, acupuncture, cannabis and supplements
- [Acupuncture, massage and traditional adjuncts in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/acupuncture-massage-and-traditional-adjuncts-in-pd/): Two older meta-analyses found no significant UPDRS advantage of real over placebo acupuncture
- [Cannabis and cannabinoids in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/cannabis-and-cannabinoids-in-pd/): The Parkinson's Foundation does not endorse use for PD symptoms or disease progression
- [Dance, tai chi, yoga, boxing and community exercise programs](https://llmsx.org/tree/dance-tai-chi-yoga-boxing-and-community-exercise-programs/): Group-based exercise modes in Parkinson's disease are described by guidelines and reviews with mixed strength
- [Exercise and physical therapy in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/exercise-and-physical-therapy-in-pd/): APTA grades aerobic exercise, resistance training and balance training as high evidence quality with strong recommendations, and flexibility exercises as low and weak
- [LSVT BIG, LSVT LOUD and speech-language therapy](https://llmsx.org/tree/lsvt-big-lsvt-loud-and-speech-language-therapy/): Two Cochrane reviews (searches to April 2011) found insufficient evidence; later meta-analyses report higher vocal loudness, while intelligibility results are mixed
- [Music, art and creative therapies in PD](https://llmsx.org/tree/music-art-and-creative-therapies-in-pd/): Meta-analyses of rhythmic auditory stimulation and music-based interventions in Parkinson's disease report positive pooled effects on gait velocity and stride length but not cadence
- [Occupational therapy, cueing and gait training](https://llmsx.org/tree/occupational-therapy-cueing-and-gait-training/): What published sources report about occupational therapy, external cueing and gait training in Parkinson's disease
- [Supplements: CoQ10, creatine, vitamin D, Mucuna and failed neuroprotectants](https://llmsx.org/tree/supplements-coq10-creatine-vitamin-d-mucuna-and-failed-neuroprotectants/): Trial evidence for supplements and failed neuroprotectants in Parkinson disease is largely negative in the sources read

## Top sources, live-checked 2026-11-27

- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9046970 (11 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9046970/): For balance training the APTA clinical practice guideline states evidence quality high and recommendation strength strong
- [nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71 (5 claims in this run)](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/Recommendations): NICE guideline NG71 (published 19 July 2017) recommends in 1.7.13 that people with Parkinson's disease be advised to take a vitamin D supplement
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530 (4 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11232530/): The PD COMM authors report that the trial could not be blinded
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7120224 (3 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7120224/): Reviews report improved motor-severity scores for exercise or physiotherapy versus control
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11001292 (2 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11001292/): The Cochrane network meta-analysis of 154 RCTs (7837 participants, mostly mild to moderate disease) found little evidence of differences between exercise types and noted
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11208974 (2 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11208974/): Trial reports and reviews state that acupuncturists cannot be blinded and that the evidence base is geographically concentrated
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3316992 (2 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3316992/): A review by LSVT researchers, two of whom disclose ownership interest in LSVT Global, Inc
- [pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5618798 (2 claims in this run)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5618798/): Meta-analytic findings on tai chi and qigong and quality of life in Parkinson's disease differ
